neighbours.label: Complementizer opening a content clause after a framing phrase (it may well be that, point out that, dass, Arabic أن/لأنّ, Japanese 、after a framing adverbial), vs 'that' as a relative pronoun or demonstrative
fire: It could well be that the early estimates were too optimistic.
It is important to note that the bridge was closed for repairs.
Sie betonte, dass die Ergebnisse noch vorläufig seien.
One might argue that the policy came far too late.
多くの場合、問題は設定ファイルにあります。
It should be stressed that no patients were harmed.
Es ist wahrscheinlich, dass der Preis weiter steigt.
Critics have long suggested that the data were incomplete.
quiet: The house that we rented had a blue door.
That car belongs to my neighbor across the street.
She liked that song more than any other.
The book that he lent me was very long.
Give me that cup on the shelf, please.
The man that fixed our roof lives nearby.
We sold the bike that had a flat tire.
That morning the river was calm and clear.

predictions: Framing phrases followed by a complementizer reach 0.15-0.3; relative and demonstrative 'that' and plain sentences stay under 0.05. The pole is broad and the median may fall short of 0.20.
notes: Card flags broad (3.6%). Top: لأنّ, Japanese 、after ほとんどの場合, مشيرا إلى أن, wenn der, daß, 'it may well be that'. Probe: may well be that 0.264, pointing out that 0.229, 、0.182, NB: 0.170, dass 0.153, Arabic إن 0.059; relative that 0.034, list 0.004.
